title: Can AI really help me price my freelance projects better? My test
excerpt: I put AI pricing tools head-to-hand with my own spreadsheet to see if they actually save time and improve quote accuracy.
metaDescription: A hands-on test of AI pricing assistants for freelancers. See how much time they save, how accurate the numbers are, and whether they win more clients.
author: Ali Hamza
coverImageAlt: Developer working at a desk with multiple screens
body:
## Why pricing feels like guesswork

I’ve spent years sending proposals that either get ghosted or end in last-minute haggling. Most freelancers rely on gut feeling, a spreadsheet, or a rule-of-thumb like "$50 per hour". That works until a client asks for a custom app or a brand overhaul and you realize you’re way off.

**Typical pain points**
- No data on market rates for niche services
- Time spent researching competitors
- Fear of pricing yourself out of a job

## What AI pricing tools promise

A few AI-driven services have appeared recently. They claim to scan job postings, past invoices, and industry reports to suggest a rate that maximizes profit while staying competitive. The most talked-about ones are:

- **RateWizard** - feeds your skill list into a language model and returns a range.
- **Bonsai AI Pricing** - integrates with your Upwork profile and suggests hourly or fixed prices.
- **FreelanceCalc** - asks for project details and spits out a quote in seconds.

I wanted to see whether the numbers are any better than my own spreadsheet.

## My experiment - setting up the test

I chose three recent project types I regularly get: a landing-page design, a small e-commerce site, and a UI kit for a SaaS startup. For each I did two things:

1. **Manual price** - I used my usual method: estimate hours, add a 20 % buffer, multiply by my base rate ($55/hr).
2. **AI price** - I fed the same brief into RateWizard and Bonsai AI Pricing, recorded the suggested hourly and total figures.

I logged project type, manual quote, AI quote, time spent calculating each, and the client’s final decision in a Google Sheet.

## Results - time, accuracy, and client reaction

### Time saved

- Manual calculation: average 12 minutes per quote.
- AI suggestion: average 3 minutes per quote (including copy-paste).

The time difference is noticeable when you’re handling many leads.

### Accuracy of the numbers

I defined “accurate” as the quote that landed within 10 % of the final agreed price. The outcomes were:

- Landing page - manual $1,320, AI $1,380, final $1,350 → both within range.
- E-commerce site - manual $4,800, AI $5,200, final $5,100 → AI a bit high but still close.
- UI kit - manual $2,200, AI $2,600, final $2,400 → AI overshot by ~8 %.

Overall the AI tools were slightly higher than my gut numbers. In my opinion that can be useful because it reduces the chance of under-pricing, though it may also turn away price-sensitive clients.

### Client reaction

Two of the four clients I pitched accepted the AI-generated quote without question. One asked for a discount, saying the number felt “premium”. The fourth client didn’t respond - a typical outcome regardless of pricing method.

## Practical takeaways

- Use AI as a sanity check, not a replacement. If the AI suggests a rate far outside your comfort zone, double-check the assumptions.
- Save the time for high-volume work. When you’re sending dozens of proposals a week, those three minutes add up.
- Combine with a simple spreadsheet. Keep your own baseline and let AI fill the gaps for niche projects you rarely do.
- Be ready to explain a higher number. Clients will ask why the quote is higher; you can point to market demand, extra research, or faster delivery.

## FAQ

**Q: Do I need a paid subscription to get reliable AI pricing?**
A: Most tools offer a free tier with limited queries per month. For occasional freelancers the free tier is enough; power users may benefit from the paid plan’s deeper data.

**Q: Can AI replace market research entirely?**
A: Not yet. AI pulls from publicly available data, which may be outdated or missing niche specifics. Treat it as a shortcut, not a crystal ball.

## Bottom line

AI pricing assistants can shave a few minutes off each quote and give you a data-backed baseline that reduces guesswork. They aren’t a magic bullet for winning every client, but they’re a useful safety net when you’re juggling many proposals.
